correctness.rationale: A C3 convex-curve chord at signed neighbor distances -v and +u crosses the inward normal at kappa uv/2+O(uv(u+v)); consecutive neighbors are a hull edge. Exact normalized nearest-gap densities converge in L1 to independent exponential densities; fixed distinct sites have a joint falling-factorial density giving total-variation independence. The exposure indicator is an a.e.-continuous threshold on the product and transfers by L1; conditioned marks inherit total-variation convergence. The Bessel survival identity is an exact convergent integral. The only n²delta_n→infty claim assumes delta_n→0, avoiding the far-boundary counterexample. The saved standalone checker independently confirmed integral, exact circle chord behavior and full polygon classification.

value.rationale: The exact critical normal-exposure probability is a naturally motivated local geometric invariant of boundary-sampled hull approximation: two O(n^-1) spacing variables create an O(n^-2) cap. This determines the complete Bessel transition, explains the rare-exposure geometry by its conditional two-exponential density, and supplies an invertible local curvature signature for known sampling density. Independent marks at fixed separated sites extend it to a local multi-probe tomography principle. It is not a routine numerical slice or a reworded fixed-n logarithmic asymptotic.
